headline: Sonny Gray deals as Red Sox shut out the Pirates at PNC
morning_brew: Finally, a clean sheet of work from the mound as Sonny Gray carved through that Pittsburgh lineup for seven innings. You could feel the focus from the first pitch, and seeing him notch his fifteenth win of the season was exactly what we needed to get back on the right track. Wilyer Abreu provided the pop we were looking for with a solo home run, making sure we didn't have to rely on a total team effort just to scrape across a few runs.

The bullpen had no interest in letting the Pirates back into it, as both Erik Miller and Chapman came out throwing gas to lock down the final two frames without a scratch. It felt damn good to watch the final inning without holding my breath, especially after the horror show we had to navigate earlier this week. You could tell the dugout had a different energy than the last couple of games, and that kind of momentum is what makes me think this squad can actually hang in the AL East hunt for a while.

My mother was actually smiling at the TV by the eighth inning, which is a rare enough occurrence that I might have to frame the moment. I haven't seen a performance that stress-free since Uncle Carmine managed to sleep through the entire 2004 postseason without knowing we won it all. We have a Sunday matinee coming up before heading back to the Fens for a homestand, and I am choosing to believe this performance was the start of a real surge. If we can keep the command sharp and the bats connected, this team might actually be worth the price of admission for the rest of August.
